reaction_equations: Au X Me Au(S2CNEt2) → Au Au(Me) (S2CNEt2) fragments
Au Au(Me) (S2CNEt2) O3 → Au Au X fragments (surface species)
surface_mechanism_description: The mechanism involves the reaction of Me2Au(S2CNEt2) with an oxidized Au surface, followed by ozone exposure that removes ligands and partially oxidizes near-surface gold. The process is self-limiting and requires ozone for activation of the growing surface to form Au-Ox species, which are then consumed during the next exposure to the Au precursor.
intermediate_species: volatile byproducts (CO, H2O, sulfur oxide, nitric oxide, etc.)
evidence: The mechanism is hypothesized based on in situ mass balance and infrared spectroscopy studies.
